rendered: The text sorts the strains into separate groups. Fully discriminated across concentrations (no cluster overlap): including P. aeruginosa, E. coli,[1] E. sakazakii, L. monocytogenes, and E. faecium, were fully distinguishable[2]. Only partial discrimination (partial cluster overlap): S. typhimurium and S. aureus[3]. Caveat: the caption of Fig. 3[4] names only the strains listed here, not E. faecium: the differentiation of P. aeruginosa,[5] E. coli, E. sakazakii and L. monocytogenes[6]. The supporting panels for the fully and partially discriminated groups are cited in the text as supplementary material, which is not in this document. Within the figure itself, the only partial overlap is in panel g, where the highest concentration pair partly overlap[7] (the figure's own pairing of panels to strains suggests E. sakazakii, which is an inference from the caption). Panels e, f and h show all five OD clusters are enclosed in non-overlapping ellipses[8].
